title: Alternating Cech total complex of a quasi-coherent complex computes derived sections
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with a finite open covering $X=\bigcup_{i=1}^r U_i$, allowing $r=0$, such that every intersection $U_{i_0}\cap\cdots\cap U_{i_p}$ indexed by a nonempty tuple (including repetitions and empty opens) is affine. Let $F^\bullet$ be an unbounded cochain complex of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-coherent] viewed by localization in $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category]. Let $T_{\mathcal U}(F^\bullet)$ and $\alpha$ be the alternating Cech total functor and its global-section augmentation of [def-sc-alternating-cech-total-complex], with Cech degree first and total differential $d_1+(-1)^p d_2$. Write $R\Gamma$ for the unbounded right derived functor of the module-valued global sections functor [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. Then (i) there exists a map $\beta_F:QT_{\mathcal U}(F^\bullet)\to R\Gamma(QF^\bullet)$ satisfying $\operatorname{IsAlternatingCechDerivedComparison}(\mathcal U,F^\bullet,\beta_F)$, the canonical-map equation through every K-injective resolution; (ii) every map satisfying that equation is an isomorphism in $D(\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X))$; and (iii) for every morphism $g:F^\bullet\to G^\bullet$ of complexes of quasi-coherent modules and comparisons $\beta_F,\beta_G$, one has $\beta_G\circ Q(T_{\mathcal U}(g))=R\Gamma(Qg)\circ\beta_F$. Thus the canonical map of Stacks lemma-alternating-cech-complex-complex is an isomorphism, functorial in $F^\bullet$, without boundedness assumptions.

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma 08C2 (cohomology-lemma-alternating-cech-complex-complex-ss) with B the affine opens, hypothesis (3) by Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01XB; as used in Perfect, Lemma 08D2

proof.text: For each degree q, the augmented alternating Cech complex of the sheaf F^q is exact: on an open U_i containing a given point, insertion of the index i gives a contracting homotopy. Since the cover is finite, the Cech direction is bounded (the terms vanish for p >= r), so these augmentations assemble naturally into a bounded filtration of the total complex.

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma 08C2, proof of the alternating Cech resolution

proof.text: For every nonempty intersection U_J, the scheme U_J is affine. Termwise affine quasi-coherent sheaf/module equivalence identifies F^\bullet|_{U_J} with the sheaf associated to its complex of sections, and the derived global-sections quasi-inverse therefore identifies RΓ(U_J,F^\bullet|_{U_J}) with Γ(U_J,F^\bullet|_{U_J}). Equivalently, the cohomology of this section complex is Γ(U_J,H^q(F^\bullet)) in every degree, naturally in F^\bullet and in restriction maps.

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma 08C2, hypothesis (3) from Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01XB

proof.text: Choose a functorial K-injective resolution F^\bullet\to I^\bullet with every term I^q an injective O_U-module, by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] (U has a set of opens, so its site is small); by [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image] (with g the structure morphism to the one-point ringed space with ring \Gamma(U,O_U)), R\Gamma(U,F^\bullet) is represented by \Gamma(U,I^\bullet), for any K-injective resolution. For each intersection U_J, the restriction I^\bullet|_{U_J} is K-injective by [lem-sc-derived-k-injective-restrict-open], so F^\bullet|_{U_J}\to I^\bullet|_{U_J} is a K-injective resolution and R\Gamma(U_J,F^\bullet|_{U_J}) is represented by \Gamma(U_J,I^\bullet); by Step 2 (U_J affine) the induced map \Gamma(U_J,F^\bullet)\to\Gamma(U_J,I^\bullet) is a quasi-isomorphism, and so is the finite product over J with |J|=p+1. Filter Tot(Cech_alt(U,F^\bullet)) and Tot(Cech_alt(U,I^\bullet)) by Cech degree (columns p\ge p_0); these filtrations are finite (r members, columns 0\le p\le r-1) and the map Tot(Cech_alt(F^\bullet))\toTot(Cech_alt(I^\bullet)) induced by F^\bullet\to I^\bullet respects them, with graded pieces the above products of quasi-isomorphisms (shifted by p). By [thm-sp-spectral-object-yields] the map induces a morphism of convergent spectral sequences, an isomorphism on E_1 hence on E_2, hence on E_\infty by [lem-sp-page-induction]; so it is an isomorphism on the finite graded pieces of H^n, hence on H^n by [lem-sp-finite-filtration-induction]: the left arrow is a quasi-isomorphism.

The right arrow \Gamma(U,I^\bullet)\toTot(Cech_alt(U,I^\bullet)) is the augmentation into column p=0. For each q, I^q is an injective O_U-module on the scheme U, so its ordered Cech complex for \mathcal U has \check H^p(\mathcal U,I^q)=0 for p>0 by [lem-weil-pbc-module-injective-open-cover-cech-acyclic], and \check H^0(\mathcal U,I^q)=I^q(U) by the sheaf axiom; by [lem-pc-alternating-cech-computes] the same holds for the alternating Cech complex, i.e. each row 0\to\Gamma(U,I^q)\to Cech_alt^0(\mathcal U,I^q)\to\cdots\to Cech_alt^{r-1}(\mathcal U,I^q)\to0 is exact. The cone of the right arrow is (up to shift and sign) the total complex of the augmented double complex, which has these exact rows and only the finitely many columns p=-1,\dots,r-1. Such a total complex is acyclic by the elementary staircase chase: given a cocycle, its component in the top column r-1 is a row boundary, so subtracting the total differential of a cochain in column r-2 removes it; descending column by column the cocycle becomes cohomologous to one concentrated in column -1, which then vanishes as the augmentation is injective; so every cocycle is a coboundary. Hence the right arrow is a quasi-isomorphism. The two quasi-isomorphisms give the zigzag Tot(Cech_alt(F^\bullet))\toTot(Cech_alt(I^\bullet))\leftarrow\Gamma(U,I^\bullet), which represents R\Gamma(U,F^\bullet) by Step 3; the composite of the left arrow with the inverse of the right arrow is by definition the canonical map, and it is an isomorphism in D(\Gamma(U,O_U)).

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma 08C2 (cohomology-lemma-alternating-cech-complex-complex-ss); injective modules are Cech acyclic (Cohomology, Lemma 01EV)

proof.text: Functoriality and independence of the resolution: the resolution F^\bullet\mapsto I^\bullet of [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] is a functor with a natural transformation from the identity, and both arrows of the zigzag are natural in the pair (F^\bullet\to I^\bullet), so for a morphism F^\bullet\to G^\bullet the zigzags form a commutative diagram and the isomorphism is natural in F^\bullet. For another K-injective resolution F^\bullet\to J^\bullet with injective terms, the comparison I^\bullet\to J^\bullet under F^\bullet of [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image] exists and is unique up to homotopy by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] (equivalently [lem-sc-kinjective-quasi-iso-comparison]) and is a homotopy equivalence, and it is compatible with both arrows of the zigzag; hence the isomorphism does not depend on the chosen resolution. The cases r=0 and F^\bullet=0 give zero total complexes and zero derived sections, agreeing with the same construction.

statement_change.old_statement: Let $U$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with a finite open covering $\mathcal U:U=\bigcup_{i=1}^rU_i$ such that $U_{i_0\ldots i_p}=U_{i_0}\cap\cdots\cap U_{i_p}$ is affine for all $p\ge0$ and all $i_0,\ldots,i_p$. Let $\mathcal F^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-modules [pqf-def-coherent], not assumed bounded in either direction. Let $\operatorname{Tot}(\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet_{\mathrm{alt}}(\mathcal U,\mathcal F^\bullet))$ be the total complex of the double complex with terms $\check{\mathcal C}^p_{\mathrm{alt}}(\mathcal U,\mathcal F^q)=\prod_{i_0<\cdots<i_p}\mathcal F^q(U_{i_0\ldots i_p})$, the alternating Cech differential $d_1$ [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex] in the $p$-direction, the differential $d_2$ induced by $\mathcal F^\bullet$ in the $q$-direction, and total differential $d_1+(-1)^pd_2$ on the $(p,q)$ term. Then there is a canonical isomorphism $\operatorname{Tot}(\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet_{\mathrm{alt}}(\mathcal U,\mathcal F^\bullet))\to R\Gamma(U,\mathcal F^\bullet)$ in $D(\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U))$ [def-pc-derived-category] [def-pc-derived-direct-image], functorial in $\mathcal F^\bullet$.
statement_change.what: The old statement described the total complex and canonical map informally, but no recorded dependency defined the alternating total functor for a general scheme or its canonical comparison. The full-site Cech complex is indexed by all tuples, and the principal-open construction is only a Spec A specialization. Quantifying over an arbitrary Tot unrelated to this construction would not express the source. The correction supplies an explicit construction and the equation through every K-injective resolution, then spells out existence, invertibility of every comparison, and functoriality; the mathematical hypotheses and result are unchanged.
